_comment: Copy this file to ~/.pi/agent/extensions/sandbox.json (global) or <cwd>/.pi/sandbox.json (project-local). Project-local values are merged on top of global. See README.md for full documentation.
_comment_mode: "default" = rules only. "advanced-secure" adds secret/credential detection. An untrusted project may move this UP (stricter), never down.

network._comment_allowedDomains: Domains that fetch_content / get_search_content may reach. Empty list = allow all.

filesystem._comment_outsideProject: Reads outside the working directory. read: allow (default) | ask | deny. allowRead = roots that never ask. The deny and ask lists below are NOT scoped to this block — they apply both inside and outside the project.
filesystem._comment_denyRead: Layer 1 (bash pre-flight AND the OS sandbox) and Layer 2 (model read tool): hard block, no prompt, no 'always'. Only key material belongs here — it can never be masked, so there is no safe way to let it through.
filesystem._comment_modelDenyRead: Layer 2 ONLY: hard block for the model's read tool while subprocesses (gh, aws, kubectl, docker) still work.
filesystem._comment_askRead: Layer 1 (bash pre-flight) AND Layer 2 (model read tool): ask before reading these, INSIDE and OUTSIDE the project. An entry without '/' matches the file name anywhere ('.env' matches <cwd>/.env and ~/x/.env); an entry with '/' or '~/' is a path pattern, and a folder entry covers every file beneath it — add one line per credential store instead of listing files ('~/.composio' works exactly like '~/.aws'). denyRead wins over askRead; filesystem.allowRead (or an overrides.allowRead entry) wins over askRead, so a noisy folder can be silenced without touching the ask list. The prompt is a single read: one file, no 'always' (ADR-019, ADR-046).
filesystem._comment_allowWrite: Layer 2: the model's write/edit tools may only write inside these roots. '.' = cwd, '~' = the home folder. Layer 1: the OS sandbox mounts only these writable. Writes are deliberately wide: a write does not leak a token, it only becomes dangerous when it lands in key material or in a file that runs code — both are held back below.
filesystem._comment_denyWrite: Layer 1 (bash pre-flight AND the OS sandbox) and Layer 2: hard block, no prompt. Key material only.
filesystem._comment_askWrite: Layer 1 (bash pre-flight) AND Layer 2: ask before writing these, so a credential file that is updated suddenly never changes under you without a prompt. Same matching as askRead: no '/' means file name anywhere, a folder entry covers everything beneath it. Shell startup files and the pi extensions folder are here because a write there becomes code execution outside the sandbox; the credential files are here because replacing them (a swapped .env, a rewritten .npmrc) redirects a tool to an attacker. denyWrite wins over askWrite, and a once/session grant answers one prompt instead of one per file.

_comment_subagent: Layer 3: stricter network policy when ctx.hasUI === false (subagents, -p mode, JSON mode).
_comment_commands: Layer 1: bash commands that can print environment variables or another process's memory (and so API keys) ask first, one run at a time, and fail closed when there is no UI. Shell wrappers are traversed: 'sh -c printenv' is detected, and 'env FOO=1 python app.py' is not a false positive.
_comment_mcp: Advanced Secure only. Tune the MCP tool-call gate (ADR-032). allowTools = exact tool names that never ask; allowPrefixes = name prefixes that never ask (e.g. 'mcp__ticktick__get_'); askTools = tool names that always ask; trustAnnotations = a server's readOnlyHint allows the call without asking; allowSimpleUpdates = narrow field updates skip the ask (default true); askThreshold = risk score at which calls ask (default 30, lower = stricter). Detected destructive calls always ask, unless an allowTools/allowPrefixes entry covers them (an explicit override). Unclassified names with a real description start at 25; a tool with no description counts as opaque and still asks. An untrusted project file may only tighten: it may add askTools, lower askThreshold, and turn allowSimpleUpdates/trustAnnotations off; allow lists need /security trust.
_comment_overrides: Additive overrides written by ask-tier prompts. You can also edit by hand. These are merged on top of the main policy. A hand-written allowRead entry wins over askRead (explicit intent); the absolute-deny tier still wins over every override.
